questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore destinations that could be interesting to move to in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The academic opportunities were very disappointing and I feel like I have wasted a semester of my education as the school did not provide proper interration to their systems in the beginning and the courses available were irrelevant or poorly executed. exchange students were prioritized last and we were kicked of courses in favor of the full time students last minute which meant I had to rearrange all my courses last minute to accommodate the time schedules. I was not able to participate in the classes I originally planned on because of poor communication and planning from the administration. 
i am sad that this semester has been wasted at an university that does not care for or cater towards exchange students. 
ultimatly is would have preferred staying at UCPH.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: almost impossible

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received one email from an angry administrator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: upon arrival the university was super unprepared and unwelcoming. the welcome reception was hostile and they immidiatly tried to scare us with how "strict" they were (did not see any of this strictness or high level of organising once during my stay). the tutors who was to show us around were uninterested and had not planned anything. I had to figure everything out on my own.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
the dutch housing market is horrible but I did manage to find housing on Facebook in one of the many rent groups. 
there are many scammers so be aware however I was able to find very good and affordable housing close to campus. I would recommend posting in one of the Facebook groups and introducing yourself. always do video calls and make sure to get a contract before sending any deposits.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived with two international girls who had studied at my university for 2 years so they were very helpfull in getting me organized and helping me around campus. I would defiantly recommend finding a place with roommates as it makes it easier to integrate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: housing available to students is very limited I would not rely on getting student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: course registration was a mess. registration was done via email so you had no idea which courses were filled and if you wanted to quit a course or an exam it was also such a long complicated process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: registration was done via email to the exchange coordinator

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: email communication

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very successful. I only got one of the courses I initially wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
be prepared the second course registration opens with our list of corses with course numbers you want so you can send the email instantly. 
also prepare an additional course list and be very thorough with the time schedule so you have a plan B

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the courses offered were ridiculous. most of the courses felt like kindergarden classes where the exams were recording a podcast and doing presentations of your favourite hero. I did not feel like my education was taken seriously and the classes were simply to easy. we were told they never give out 9 and 10s (the highest grade) however all exchange students got those grades with minimum effort.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the university only offers master level courses to exchange students which is fine as the courses really are not too hard. however you do need prior knowledge in EU law.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
doing a comparison of this would be like comparing Messi to my 10 year old little brother at the school playground. 
it does not compare.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Wicked legal ethics, Dutch law and legal culture, European integration and policy, Legal theory and methods and Comparative constitutional law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend European integration and policy as the profferers in this course are bright, professional, dedicated and motivating. this class was above any of the courses I took at EUR. 
it was one of the more demanding courses and required a lot of reading and preparing compared to the other courses. however compared to the courses at UCPH it was similar in preparation

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The Netherlands is a very affordable country to live in so any unexpected costs were very manageable

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
food, restaurants, bars, activities are super affordable so I would defiantly recommend trying all the local spots while you are here as you will get a lot for your money. 
transportation is on the other hand super expensive if you want to take the train. so I would recommend using the tram or metro to get around as that is fairly priced. I would also recommend getting a student mobility travel card as you save money on transportation using that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
EUR offers many fun activities and has a great sports program that I would recommend getting if ou are into classes like yoga, boxing, spinning, zumba etc. 
they also have a gym that is nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there are different athletics clubs like running.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: joining the sports program.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend visiting the campus bar after school.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: dutch people are a hit or miss. if you find the more open minded people they can be super nice and welcoming however frat culture is a big part of dutch culture and in those circles money, status and appearance is important.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to the local bars. drinking and partying is a very big part of their culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found dutch people to be very rude and unbecoming. they justify it with the fact that they are just straightforward however I found that their perception of being "blunt" was making fun of race, gender, appearance and social status and I don't see where the fun in that is.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated their food and wine culture. rotterdam is filled with amazing and affordable food opportunities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
honestly I wish someone told me not to go. if you want to have a fun year filled with partying, food and culture stains in rotterdam is a great opportunity however if you actually value your academics then this is not the place for you. the university is unserious and you will get treated as a last priority. 
however if you choose to go I would spend a lot of time preparing and reading up on the "how to's" of the university as you will not get any help from them. preferably reaching to to a former student and hearing them out. 
secondly enjoy all the activities offered at EUR and participate in as much as possible to get the real EUR experience. 
and lastly travel around The Netherlands and to Belgium it is easy and affordable and there is so much to see.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: prepare, prepare, prepare

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: really using the opportunity to explore The Netherlands and experience so many great things

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: trying to get the university to work with you instead of against you

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
